Watch one sunflower move from seed to germination, seedling, leafy growth, flower bud, full bloom, pollination, mature seed head, and the end of its annual life. A sunflower head is made of many individual florets, and each successfully pollinated disk floret can develop a seed.

instagram.body:
A sunflower's bright bloom is only the middle of its story. The open head contains hundreds of tiny florets. After pollination, the ray flowers fade, seeds fill the disk, the heavy head bends, and the annual plant eventually dries and dies.

Sunflowers also grow in Basil Community Garden: https://basilcommunitygarden.com/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=botanical_lifecycle&utm_content=sunflower_20260804

reddit.headline: The full sunflower lifecycle, from one seed to a mature seed head
reddit.body:
This silent sequence follows one common sunflower through its entire annual lifecycle. The head is a cluster of many flowers: pollination moves across the open disk, the yellow ray flowers later fade, and the disk fills with achenes we usually call sunflower seeds. After those seeds mature, the annual plant reaches its final dry stage.
